IEA Greenhouse Gas R&D Programme (IEA GHG) (2008). CO2 Capture in the Cement Industry. Technical Study, Report Number 2008/3, July 2008. Cheltenham: IEA GHG. Prepared by Mott MacDonald Ltd (Brighton, UK; job 234996) - D. Barker, D. Holmes, J. Hunt, P. Napier-Moore, S. Turner and M. Clark (Whitehopleman); IEA GHG manager J. Davison.

Loaded: the 1 Mt/y UK new-build reference plant without capture, the post-combustion MEA case (source split: cement-plant column on kiln_dry-precalciner_ccs-diffuse, post-combustion-plant column on capture-unit_amine, totals on a whole-plant row marked INCLUDES CAPTURE), the oxy-combustion (precalciner only) case (cement-plant column on kiln_oxy-fuel, oxy plant column on a capture-unit row, totals on a whole-plant row), the 95%-capture MEA modelling, KS-1, low-sulphur/external-steam, co-location and Asian 3 Mt/y sensitivities (whole-plant capex/fixed from the App. F cash-flow sheets), the ASU, and literature kiln-route fuel ranges. All absolute costs (EUR M) are put per t/yr of clinker (910,000 t/y; Asian 2,730,000) or per t/yr CO2 captured with the formula shown; levelized costs stay per t CEMENT as printed. Fuel energy derived from printed tonnages x printed LHVs (App. A/B), matching the printed MW. Not loaded: +/-25% and other single-parameter sensitivities (selected in other-values), stream tables (App. C-E), emission limits, pre-combustion and novel capture review (Sect. 3), retrofit and capture-ready text. Locator: printed page numbers (Overview p.1-8; main report S-x, 2-x ... 10-x; App. letter-x); PDF page = printed + offset (main report p.4-1 = PDF 73).

(6) Exchange rate 1.389 USD/EUR (p.5-1) vs 1.5 (Overview). (7) MEA make-up 2,400 t/y (Table 4-3) vs 2,242 (Table 5-7); FGD limestone 12,795 vs 12,830.
